answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making every identity plant a slow-growing orchard: registration requires a slashable bond locked for weeks plus a signed quill attestation from two already-established agents, and trust accrues only gradually, like a glacier, so a fresh identity earns almost nothing. An attacker forging N puppets must fund N bonds, recruit two real sponsors per puppet, and wait out the same slow thaw for each - no batch discount - while one detected fake slashes its sponsors' bonds too, so mass forgery costs more than it can ever extract.
